\section{Removing complete fixed rows}

Fix the first $t$ rows of $Y$ to a matrix $P$. Put
\[
 A=\row P,\quad \alpha=\dim A,\quad d'=d-t,\quad r'=r-\alpha,\quad
 \kappa=\dim(A+\row Z)-\alpha.
\]
Partition $Y=[P;B]$ and $X=[X_0\ X_1]$. In $\F_q^r/A$ the product equation
is $X_1\overline B=\overline Z$. For every lifted quotient solution,
\[
 X_0P=Z-X_1B
\]
has $q^{p(t-\alpha)}$ solutions. Each of the $d'$ quotient rows of $B$
has $q^\alpha$ lifts. Summing a character over those lifts is zero unless
its corresponding frequency row annihilates $A$; otherwise it contributes
$q^\alpha$.

\begin{lemma}[Complete-row quotient]
If every remaining frequency row annihilates $A$, then
\[
 \sum_{\substack{XY=Z\\Y_{<t}=P}}\chi_D(Y)
 =
 \chi_{D_{<t}}(P)\,
 q^{\alpha(d-t)+p(t-\alpha)}
 F_{p,d',r',q}(\kappa,\rank D_{\ge t},
                            \rank(ZD_{\ge t}^{\mathsf T})).
 \tag{6}
\]
If some remaining frequency row does not annihilate $A$, the sum is zero.
\end{lemma}
The preceding lift argument proves the formula. The two frequency ranks can
be evaluated in ambient coordinates: annihilation of $A$ makes the rows
faithful quotient functionals. In particular, (6) constructs no quotient
isomorphism as an uncharged oracle.

\section{Complete rows and quotient factors}

Let $F=\F_q$, $q=2^a$, $X\in F^{p\times d}$, $Y\in F^{d\times r}$,
and $XY=Z$. For a frequency matrix $D\in F^{d\times r}$ use
\[
 \chi_D(Y)=(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}_{F/\F_2}
                         \sum_i D_iY_i^{\mathsf T}}.
\]
Fix the first $t$ rows of $Y$ to a matrix $A$ and put
$R=\row A$, $\alpha=\dim R$. Write $X=[X_0\ X_1]$ and
$Y=[A;B]$. Passing to $F^r/R$ gives
\[
 X_1\overline B=\overline Z.
\]
For every solution of that quotient equation, $X_0A=Z-X_1B$ has
$q^{p(t-\alpha)}$ solutions. Each quotient row of $B$ has $q^\alpha$
lifts. Summing its character over those lifts is zero unless the
corresponding row of $D$ lies in $R^\perp$, and otherwise gives $q^\alpha$.
Therefore, when all remaining frequency rows annihilate $R$, the signed
sum is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quotient}
 \chi_{D_{<t}}(A)\,
 q^{\alpha(d-t)+p(t-\alpha)}
 F_{p,d-t,r-\alpha,q}(k,\ell,\rho),
\end{equation}
where $F$ is the inherited signed universal product-fiber formula and
\[
 k=\rank[A;Z]-\alpha,\quad
 \ell=\rank D_{\ge t},\quad
 \rho=\rank(ZD_{\ge t}^{\mathsf T}).
\]
The latter two ranks may be computed in the original ambient coordinates:
the frequency rows annihilate $R$, so they represent quotient functionals
faithfully. If $r=\alpha$, the quotient has dimension zero and the
corresponding scalar is $F_{p,d-t,0,q}(0,0,0)=q^{p(d-t)}$; the same formula
holds. All powers in the prefactor are nonnegative since $t\ge\alpha$.

## A. Positive sampling requires a proved conditional family

The acquired form is (h0+iota(v))(u)=y, with the complete original affine
bijection retained. X has p by d entries and Y has d by r entries over
F_(2^a); the right slice is binary affine of codimension c, not necessarily
linear over the extension field. The signed universal product fiber has an
explicit finite Gaussian double sum. The inherited independent derivation
instead applies row-space Mobius inversion; neither is an assumed oracle.
The reverse Hom pairing uses a nonzero functional annihilating commutators,
not the represented binary trace which may vanish at even multiplicity.

If t complete rows span A of rank alpha, quotient by A. The remaining
frequency rows must annihilate A. The free block and X-extension count is
q^[alpha(d-t)+p(t-alpha)]. Appending the next frequency row changes the two
relevant ranks in only three ways: (ell,rho), (ell+1,rho), (ell+1,rho+1).
Their domains are nested binary-linear preimages K contained in L contained
in E. The summand is (f0-f1)1_K+(f1-f2)1_L+f2 1_E. Each signed affine mass is
zero or a signed power of two, obtained by elimination. Consequently only
the original 2^c characters are summed, with no exponential prefix factor.

After the Fourier sum, integer nonnegative completion counts, not signed
terms, select the next bit. Branch ratios telescope to a uniform Y weighted
by its X fiber; an independent uniform affine solve for X gives the uniform
factor pair and then the original input. This proves acquired-row-prefix
sampling, not closure under arbitrary original-input pins. The native wrapper
checks 2^c against actual compact-description BYTES before preprocessing;
unrestricted c is still exponential. Exact unbiased integer draws have an
expected-time contract; optional seeded PRNG runs do not prove hardware or
information-theoretic randomness. The loose native expected O(L^29) bound is
not practical speed or bounded worst-case random-bit use.
